belief: A good woman puts everyone else first.
origins: Girls often learn to be helpful, agreeable, and self-sacrificing. Mothers modeling endless giving, church examples of serving, and praise for “selflessness” can leave women exhausted and resentful, unsure whether they are permitted needs of their own.
teaches: Paul urges, “in humility consider others more important than yourselves. Each of you should look not only to your own interests, but also to the interests of others.” Notice “not only.” Jesus said to love your neighbor “as yourself,” which assumes caring for yourself. Jesus Himself withdrew to rest and pray. The woman of Proverbs 31 buys fields, manages her household, and “opens her mouth with wisdom.” Serving others is godly. Erasing yourself is not what Scripture asks.
self_statements: If I take time for me, I am selfish.
A good woman never says no.
I am responsible for others’ happiness.
errors: Believing I am either selfless or selfish.
Assuming others will think I am selfish.
Feeling guilty and concluding that I am wrong to rest.
Predicting that everything will fall apart if I say no.
questions: Who taught me that goodness means self-erasure?
What does Scripture say about looking to others’ interests “not only” my own?
What happens to me when I never rest?
What would I tell my daughter or a friend?
What would a healthy balance look like?
What is one need I can meet this week?
truth: I am a person made in God’s image, with worth and needs. Serving is good, and so is rest, boundaries, and care for myself. Loving my neighbor as myself includes myself.
hw_truths: I am made in God’s image.
Look to others’ interests, not only my own.
log: Each week, note one need you met and one kind no.
actions: Write what you need in body, mind, and spirit.
prayer: Lord, I have poured out until I am empty. Teach me to serve with joy, rest with permission, and care for the life You gave me. Amen.
hw_questions: What happens when I never rest?
What would I tell a friend?
name_example: Sarah can write: “I can care for others’ interests and my own.”
